Centre for Epilepsy

Neurosciences Division 

Clinic Date: 02 October 2025 

Dr Fiona  
Centre for Epilepsy  
Queen Square, London WC1N 3BG  

Dear Dr Fiona,                                                                                                         

Amelia Hart, DOB: 22-11-1991, Hospital No: Q572639 NHS No. 9182736450  
Flat 3, 28 Rosemead Road, London, SW12 9JP  

Epilepsy 

Medication: Ongoing Levetiracetam since March 2025  

Levetiracetam 500 mg twice a day (patient-reported adherence, no missed doses in the last 8 weeks) 

Levetiracetam Blood Level:  

20 September 2025: 14 µg/mL (laboratory therapeutic reference 12–46 µg/mL). Dose 500 mg twice a day.  

Seizures: She may remain seizure-free for up to 4 month, but then will experience clusters of 5 seizures in a single day. These clusters have reduced in intensity and recovery time over the last two episodes, with no injuries or prolonged post-ictal confusion reported. No clear auras or focal features described. 

I reviewed Amelia Hart today in follow-up. Since relocating at work from the hot cookline to a prep area with improved ventilation, she reports fewer heat and fume triggers, better sleep continuity, and reduced daytime fatigue. She has maintained occupational stability for three consecutive months and has not required emergency attendance during this period. Family observations corroborate shorter events and faster return to baseline. 

We discussed ongoing self-monitoring, hydration, and maintaining regular sleep. She prefers to continue with her current regimen given recent improvement and lack of adverse effects (no mood change, dizziness, or rash). Safety advice around bathing and working near sharp implements was reiterated. I will continue to track cluster frequency and duration using her seizure diary and request repeat serum level if any breakthrough outside the pattern occurs. 

Plan:  
- Continue Levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily.  
- Maintain seizure diary with specific note of potential heat or exertion triggers.  
- Workplace adjustments to remain in place; no further changes needed currently.  
- Telephone review in 3 months, sooner if clusters increase or if injuries occur. 

Overall, there is a positive trend with sustained stability in recent months, likely supported by improved work environment and consistent medication adherence. 

Yours sincerely
cases.gold_note: Gold is the two-part cluster label `1 cluster per 4 month, 5 per cluster`.
cases.fixture_note: Development letter from Gan 2026 dev750. Model outputs are a Grok 4.6 replay; no live call is made. Downstream stages are the selected implementation.
cases.story: Quiet interval and cluster grammar compete; this Grok replay does not assemble the two-part gold.
cases.gold_reference: She may remain seizure-free for up to 4 month, but then will experience clusters of 5 seizures in a single day

card_why.rules: Rules match the cluster count to the four-month quiet window.
card_why.llm: The model kept only `5 per cluster`; selected-evidence repair emptied that to no seizure frequency reference.
card_why.llm_with_rules: The model wrote a cluster-after-quiet phrase; selected-evidence repair then kept only the quiet interval.

cases.mechanism: The letter states a seizure-free interval of up to four months and clusters of five seizures in a day. Gold needs both parts. On this Grok replay, rules get the two-part label; the model-led methods collapse to the cluster count or the quiet interval.

runs.one_sentence: Deterministic rules find every seizure-frequency statement in the letter, normalize them, pick one as the current answer, and render it as a Gan label.
runs.correctness_note: purist predicted seizure_freq_more1mon_less1week vs gold seizure_freq_more1mon_less1week; pragmatic predicted seizure_frequent vs gold seizure_frequent

cases.note_text:
Epilepsy Centre

Neurosciences Division


From: Dr Priya Shah (KING'S COLLEGE HOSPITAL NHS FOUNDATION TRUST)
Sent: 27 June 2019 11:20
To: epilepsy.clinic@nhs.net
Cc: Dr Michael Turner (KING'S COLLEGE HOSPITAL NHS FOUNDATION TRUST); Dr Helen Brooks (KING'S COLLEGE HOSPITAL NHS FOUNDATION TRUST)
Subject: Treatment review and guidance

Hi Priya

Epilepsy Diagnosis:

Generalised epilepsy


Present Medication:

1. Sodium Valproate 300 mg in the morning and 500 mg at night
2. Lamotrigine 50 mg twice daily


Present Seizure Frequency:

Patient reports frequent petit mal recently, particularly on waking and during periods of prolonged screen use at work. No generalised tonic–clonic seizures for over a year.


Plan of Action:

The patient describes increasing brief absence episodes over the past six weeks, with no clear illness, sleep deprivation, or missed doses identified. They feel work-related visual strain and stress may be contributory. Given the pattern in generalised epilepsy, I recommend a cautious optimisation of lamotrigine while maintaining sodium valproate.

Please adjust Lamotrigine as follows: increase to 75 mg twice daily for two weeks, then to 100 mg twice daily thereafter, provided no rash or adverse effects occur. Continue Sodium Valproate at the current dose. If sedation or tremor emerge, please let me know, as we may need to fine-tune the evening valproate dose.

I have advised the patient on regular sleep, breaks from screen exposure (20–20–20 rule), and to keep a seizure diary documenting time of day, precipitating factors, and functional impact. They will also arrange an optometry review to reduce visual strain at work.

I will review them in clinic in three months. If the frequent petit mal recently persist despite the above, we will consider substituting valproate with ethosuximide or adjusting therapy toward levetiracetam, balancing efficacy and tolerability.

With best wishes

cases.note_text:
Clinic date 25/09/2018
 
Re          Mr Owen Owens	30/06/1968
 
Dear doctor,

Diagnosis: Symptomatic structural focal epilepsy
		Area of ischaemic damage left inferior frontal lobe
		Significant anxiety and depression
 
I reviewed this 50 year old man, together with his wife, in clinic today. He was well from an epilepsy point of view until he had a seizure last month. His wife heard a bang from the next room and went in to see him unconsciouss on the floor. He was stiff, his eyes were open and he made unusual groaning noises before starting to shake. This lasted about 40 seconds before he went to a “deep sleep”. It took him several hours to recover fully. Mr Owens himself remembers his right leg twitching before he lost consciousness. I think therefore that this was a focal to bilateral convulsive seizures. As you recall Mr Owens has had focal motor seizures in the past where he has had jerking of his right leg. These were happening frequently before he started the medication. The last event was probably 10 months ago. He has had one previous focal to bilateral convulsive seizure at the time of diagnosis of his epilepsy in May 2017. As you will recall his MRI at the time was abnormal with an area of ischaemic damage in the left inferior frontal lobe. This is the probable cause of his epilepsy. An EEG in 2017 did show some left sided sharp waves.

He is currently taking lamotrigine 75mg twice a day and given the recent seizure I would be very grateful if you could increase this by 25mg every fortnight to 100mg twice a day. It can be increased further if necessary in a similar way. Previously he tried levetiracetam but this made his mood worse.

Mr Owens has ongoing problems with his mood and finds it very difficult to leave the house. He has found anti-depressants useful in the past and I would be very grateful if you could reassess him from his mental health point of view. There is no contraindication to treatment with anti-depressants if necessary.
Mr Owens is still managing to work as an accountant and he is aware of the DVLA driving regulations. He is currently drinking around 40units of alcohol a week. We had a chat about the effects of alcohol and I would advise that he reduces his intake to the recommended 14 units of alcohol per week with a few alcohol free days.
I will ask the epilepsy nurses to review again. 
Yours

"Clinic date 25/09/2018\n \nRe          Mr Owen Owens\t30/06/1968\n \nDear doctor,\n\nDiagnosis: Symptomatic structural focal epilepsy\n\t\tArea of ischaemic damage left inferior frontal lobe\n\t\tSignificant anxiety and depression\n \nI reviewed this 50 year old man, together with his wife, in clinic today. He was well from an epilepsy point of view until he had a seizure last month. His wife heard a bang from the next room and went in to see him unconsciouss on the floor. He was stiff, his eyes were open and he made unusual groaning noises before starting to shake. This lasted about 40 seconds before he went to a “deep sleep”. It took him several hours to recover fully. Mr Owens himself remembers his right leg twitching before he lost consciousness. I think therefore that this was a focal to bilateral convulsive seizures. As you recall Mr Owens has had focal motor seizures in the past where he has had jerking of his right leg. These were happening frequently before he started the medication. The last event was probably 10 months ago. He has had one previous focal to bilateral convulsive seizure at the time of diagnosis of his epilepsy in May 2017. As you will recall his MRI at the time was abnormal with an area of ischaemic damage in the left inferior frontal lobe. This is the probable cause of his epilepsy. An EEG in 2017 did show some left sided sharp waves.\n\nHe is currently taking lamotrigine 75mg twice a day and given the recent seizure I would be very grateful if you could increase this by 25mg every fortnight to 100mg twice a day. It can be increased further if necessary in a similar way. Previously he tried levetiracetam but this made his mood worse.\n\nMr Owens has ongoing problems with his mood and finds it very difficult to leave the house. He has found anti-depressants useful in the past and I would be very grateful if you could reassess him from his mental health point of view. There is no contraindication to treatment with anti-depressants if necessary.\nMr Owens is still managing to work as an accountant and he is aware of the DVLA driving regulations. He is currently drinking around 40units of alcohol a week. We had a chat about the effects of alcohol and I would advise that he reduces his intake to the recommended 14 units of alcohol per week with a few alcohol free days.\nI will ask the epilepsy nurses to review again. \nYours\n\n"}

lobe\n\t\tSignificant anxiety and depression\n \nI reviewed this 50 year old man, together with his wife, in clinic today. He was well from an epilepsy point of view until he had a seizure last month. His wife heard a bang from the next room and went in to see him unconsciouss on the floor. He was stiff, his eyes were open and he made unusual groaning noises before starting to shake. This lasted about 40 seconds before he went to a “deep sleep”. It took him several hours to recover fully. Mr Owens himself remembers his right leg twitching before he lost consciousness. I think therefore that this was a focal to bilateral convulsive seizures. As you recall Mr Owens has had focal motor seizures in the past where he has had jerking of his right leg. These were happening frequently before he started the medication. The last event was probably 10 months ago. He has had one previous focal to bilateral convulsive seizure at the time of diagnosis of his epilepsy in May 2017. As you will recall his MRI at the time was abnormal with an area of ischaemic damage in the left inferior frontal lobe. This is the probable cause of his epilepsy. An EEG in 2017 did show some left sided sharp waves.\n\nHe is currently taking lamotrigine 75mg twice a day and given the recent seizure I would be very grateful if you could increase this by 25mg every fortnight to 100mg twice a day. It can be increased further if necessary in a similar way. Previously he tried levetiracetam but this made his mood worse.\n\nMr Owens has ongoing problems with his mood and finds it very difficult to leave the house. He has found anti-depressants useful in the past and I would be very grateful if you could reassess him from his mental health point of view. There is no contraindication to treatment with anti-depressants if necessary.\nMr Owens is still managing to work as an accountant and he is aware of the DVLA driving regulations. He is currently drinking around 40units of alcohol a week. We had a chat about the effects of alcohol and I would advise that he reduces his intake to the recommended 14 units of alcohol per week with a few alcohol free days.\nI will ask the epilepsy nurses to review again. \nYours\n\n"}

"Clinic date 25/09/2018\n \nRe          Mr Owen Owens\t30/06/1968\n \nDear doctor,\n\nDiagnosis: Symptomatic structural focal epilepsy\n\t\tArea of ischaemic damage left inferior frontal lobe\n\t\tSignificant anxiety and depression\n \nI reviewed this 50 year old man, together with his wife, in clinic today. He was well from an epilepsy point of view until he had a seizure last month. His wife heard a bang from the next room and went in to see him unconsciouss on the floor. He was stiff, his eyes were open and he made unusual groaning noises before starting to shake. This lasted about 40 seconds before he went to a “deep sleep”. It took him several hours to recover fully. Mr Owens himself remembers his right leg twitching before he lost consciousness. I think therefore that this was a focal to bilateral convulsive seizures. As you recall Mr Owens has had focal motor seizures in the past where he has had jerking of his right leg. These were happening frequently before he started the medication. The last event was probably 10 months ago. He has had one previous focal to bilateral convulsive seizure at the time of diagnosis of his epilepsy in May 2017. As you will recall his MRI at the time was abnormal with an area of ischaemic damage in the left inferior frontal lobe. This is the probable cause of his epilepsy. An EEG in 2017 did show some left sided sharp waves.\n\nHe is currently taking lamotrigine 75mg twice a day and given the recent seizure I would be very grateful if you could increase this by 25mg every fortnight to 100mg twice a day. It can be increased further if necessary in a similar way. Previously he tried levetiracetam but this made his mood worse.\n\nMr Owens has ongoing problems with his mood and finds it very difficult to leave the house. He has found anti-depressants useful in the past and I would be very grateful if you could reassess him from his mental health point of view. There is no contraindication to treatment with anti-depressants if necessary.\nMr Owens is still managing to work as an accountant and he is aware of the DVLA driving regulations. He is currently drinking around 40units of alcohol a week. We had a chat about the effects of alcohol and I would advise that he reduces his intake to the recommended 14 units of alcohol per week with a few alcohol free days.\nI will ask the epilepsy nurses to review again. \nYours\n\n"}

cases.note_text:
NHS No 4961112233
Date 19/9/2016


Dear Dr

r.e. Mr Laurence Harris.  D.O.B.: 10/1/1960
40, Hospital pass, Johnstown. SA5 3ZZ

Diagnosis	1. Dissociative seizures (non-epileptic attacks)
		2. Symptomatic structural epilepsy secondary to previous cerebral abcess

Medication:	Levetiracetam 1000mg bd
		

I reviewed this 56-year-old man in clinic today. He has been previously reviewed by other members of the epilepsy department. As you know his epilepsy started 16 years ago, 2 months after having brain surgery. This was to drain a right frontal lobe brain abcess. He used to have focal motor seizures without changes in awareness, these would involve his left arm twitching with retained awareness. He used to gets these every month but has not had a seizure like this for around two years now. He has previously had focal to bilateral convulsive seizures. his last one was on Christmas day 2009.

He continues to get dissociative seizures which are brought on by stress. They are different to his epilepsy seizures, are longer and he will have his eyes closed during them. Currently he his having dissociative seizures around twice every week.

He was born normally has not had any febrile seizures or significant cerebral infections apart from the brain abscess. He has not been able to work since his brain operation, previously he worked as a fork lift truck driver. He does not smoke but drinks around 20 units of alcohol per week (10 pints of mild). He has taken amphetamines in the past but has not done so since his operation. There is no relevant family history. He is not driving at the moment. He lives with his wife and 19 year old daughter.

There was a mild left hemiparesis but otherwise his neurological examination was normal.

A MRI two years ago showed an area of gliosis in the right frontal lobe secondary to his previous surgery.

Comments
Mr Harris does have epilepsy as a result of his brain surgery and has a tendency for ongoing epileptic seizures. He therefore needs to stay on anti-epileptic medication. However his main issue at the moment are dissociative seizures. We went over these and I explained that they are not caused by electrical disturbance that cause epileptic seizures but instead can be thought of as the brain “dissociating”. The website www.nonepilepticattacks.info is an excellent source of information and I will also re-refer him to neuro-psychology who have been useful in the past.
cases.gold_note: Gold separates symptomatic structural epilepsy from dissociative attacks and keeps each frequency on its own diagnosis.
cases.fixture_note: Development letter from ExECTv2 dev140. Model outputs are a Luna Compact replay; Grok Compact is not on disk yet. No live call is made. Downstream stages are the selected implementation.
cases.story: Epileptic and dissociative diagnoses share the letter; rates must stay attached to the right one.

card_why.rules: Rules extract both diagnoses and their separate rates.
card_why.llm: The model may attach the weekly rate to epilepsy.
card_why.llm_with_rules: The diagnosis lens rewrites the structural-epilepsy phrase; the other three families assemble without a further rewrite.

cases.mechanism_title: Which rate belongs to which diagnosis
cases.mechanism: The letter states structural epilepsy that is now quiet and dissociative attacks twice a week. A model that puts the weekly rate on epilepsy has mixed the two diagnoses. The diagnosis and seizure-frequency lenses exist to keep those facts apart.

manifests.one_sentence: Deterministic rules find every seizure-frequency statement in the letter, normalize them, pick one as the current answer, and render it as a Gan label.
manifests.sixty_second: No model is involved. Pattern rules read the letter and emit candidate seizure-frequency events, each carrying its own evidence span. A normalization stage converts the free text of each candidate into a comparable monthly rate. A selection stage then applies the Gan clinical policy - prefer a current, typical, overall burden - to choose one winning event, and renders it as a Gan label string. An evidence-and-trace check confirms the rendered answer is still supported by the span the rule matched. Finally the single label is projected into the Purist and Pragmatic scoring categories. Every clinical choice in this method belongs to a named rule group, so any error can be attributed to a rule rather than to a model.
manifests.scored_representation: One Gan label string per letter, projected to a Purist and a Pragmatic category.

stages.name: Extract candidate events
stages.operation: Run the seizure-frequency pattern rules over the note text and emit every candidate event with its evidence span, temporality, and certainty.
stages.input_type: note text (str) plus source row index
stages.input_example: "He reports about two seizures per month, though he had seven so far this year."
stages.output_example: two candidate events: 'about two seizures per month' (rate, current) and 'seven so far this year' (count, year-to-date)
stages.paper_wording: Deterministic pattern rules extract candidate seizure-frequency events with source-anchored evidence spans.
stages.notes: This is where clinical content originates in the rules-only method: a phrase the rules do not match cannot be selected later.

stages.name: Normalize candidate events
stages.operation: Convert each candidate's source phrase into a comparable normalized rate and label form without choosing between candidates.
stages.input_example: 'about two seizures per month'
stages.paper_wording: Candidate events are normalized to a common rate representation before selection.
stages.notes: Normalization is representation-only by contract: it must not drop or reorder candidates. tests/test_gan2026_normalize_governance.py is the governing constraint.

stages.name: Select the current event and render the label
stages.operation: Apply the Gan clinical selection policy to choose one event as the current answer, then render it as a Gan label string with rationale and evidence.
stages.input_example: two normalized events: 2 per month (typical, current) and 7 per year (year-to-date)
stages.output_example: final_label '2 per month', evidence 'about two seizures per month'
stages.paper_wording: A deterministic selection policy chooses one current event and renders the final label.
stages.notes: This stage owns the prediction. The competing-rate policies catalogued in docs/research/shared/clinical_selection_policy_catalog_2026-07-31.md fire here.

stages.name: Check evidence and clinical trace
stages.operation: Confirm the rendered answer is still supported by the matched span and build the clinical assessment trace; record which ablation switches were disabled.
stages.input_type: note text, FinalSelection, CandidateSet, selected index
stages.input_example: final_label '2 per month' with evidence 'about two seizures per month'
stages.paper_wording: Each selected answer is checked against its source span before scoring.

stages.name: Project to Purist and Pragmatic scoring
stages.operation: Map the predicted and gold monthly frequencies into the Purist and Pragmatic categories and compare.
stages.input_type: predicted label and gold monthly frequency
stages.input_example: predicted 2.0 per month, gold 2.0 per month
stages.output_type: per-row category comparison and aggregate metrics
stages.paper_wording: Predictions are scored under the Purist and Pragmatic category projections.
stages.notes: Two letters with different clinical answers can score identically if both land in the same category. The scorer, not the pipeline, decides that.

manifests.one_sentence: One model call reads the letter and returns the final Gan label directly; deterministic code then repairs, validates, and scores that answer.
manifests.sixty_second: The prompt carries the Gan rule taxonomy, and the model returns a single decision object: final label, evidence, answer kind, selected seizure type, time window, confidence, and rationale. The model owns the clinical decision - no deterministic extractor proposes candidates. After the call, code repairs JSON dialect and schema shape, validates the decision against the schema, and then applies one selected-evidence label repair. That repair is not cosmetic: it can change the final label when the model's label disagrees with the evidence span it quoted. The repaired label is checked for scorability and evidence containment, then projected into the Purist and Pragmatic categories. The honest summary is that the model makes the clinical decision and exactly one deterministic stage can overrule its wording.
manifests.prediction_owner: the model (stage gan.llm.model_call), with one deterministic override at gan.llm.selected_evidence_repair
manifests.scored_representation: One Gan label string per letter, projected to a Purist and a Pragmatic category.

stages.input_example: note text plus taxonomy instructions
stages.output_example: {"final_label": "2 per month", "evidence": "about two seizures per month", ...}
stages.paper_wording: A single language-model call produces the final seizure-frequency label and its supporting evidence.
stages.notes: This is the prediction boundary. row_trace.model_prediction.record retains the model's answer before any deterministic stage touches it.

stages.name: Repair JSON dialect and payload shape
stages.operation: Recover the JSON object from the raw output, repair Python-literal dialect, fix a known rationale key typo, coerce rule-family fields, and drop unsupported keys.

stages.output_example: a dict matching the decision schema keys

The row trace labels its rule_category 'benchmark_format', which understates it; the manifest is the authority. Reported in finding 4 of the 2026-07-30 review.

stages.paper_wording: Evidence is required to be an exact substring of the source note.

manifests.one_sentence: The model extracts the event history and chooses an answer; deterministic rules then check and sometimes correct that answer.
manifests.sixty_second: One structured call returns two linked objects: an event ledger of source-near seizure-frequency facts, and a selection naming which event IDs won, the answer kind, the final label, evidence, confidence, and rationale. The model therefore makes the initial clinical selection - this is the single most misread fact about the method. Deterministic code then repairs JSON and schema, normalizes every event to a comparable rate, resolves an initial label from the model's chosen events, and runs ten named repair families in a fixed order. Each family can rewrite the final label, and each records a named event when it fires, so a changed answer is always attributable to one rule. The repaired label is checked for scorability and exact evidence, then projected to Purist and Pragmatic categories. Model owns the first answer; rules own every subsequent change to it.
manifests.prediction_owner: the model proposes and selects (gan.llm_with_rules.model_call); ten deterministic repair families may change the answer afterwards
manifests.scored_representation: One Gan label string per letter, projected to a Purist and a Pragmatic category.

stages.operation: Render the note text and the event-ledger schema into the prompt input for one structured call.

stages.paper_wording: A single prompt requests a structured event ledger and an explicit selection.

stages.name: Model extracts events and selects the answer
stages.operation: One structured call returns an event ledger plus a selection naming selected_event_ids, final_kind, final_label, evidence, confidence, and rationale.
stages.input_example: note text plus the event-ledger schema
stages.paper_wording: A single language-model call produces a structured event ledger and an explicit selection of the current event.
stages.notes: The model, not a deterministic selector, makes the initial event selection. Finding 5 of the 2026-07-30 review reported a teaching fixture that attributed this to a deterministic component.

stages.name: Repair JSON dialect and payload shape
stages.operation: Recover the JSON object, repair Python-literal dialect, repair the selected-answer payload shape, quarantine events that fail event-level validation, and drop unsupported keys.
stages.input_example: output using True/None, or an events list containing one malformed entry
stages.output_example: a dict matching the structured extraction schema
stages.paper_wording: Malformed model output is repaired at the transport and schema level only.
stages.notes: Event quarantine removes entries that cannot validate. It is transport-level by contract, but it does reduce the ledger the model's selection can point at; quarantine notes are retained in parse_errors.

stages.name: Format-only retry (local models)
stages.operation: For local ollama-served models whose first output was unparseable, ask for a format-only repair of the same content and re-enter the parse path; the retry is accepted only if it validates.
stages.input_type: malformed raw output plus the target schema
stages.input_example: truncated JSON from a local model
stages.output_type: repaired JSON (str) or a rejection note
stages.paper_wording: Local-model outputs that fail to parse receive one format-only repair attempt, accepted only when it validates.
stages.notes: Conditional. Fires only in live mode for models whose name starts with ollama_chat/.

stages.name: Validate the extraction schema
stages.operation: Validate the repaired payload against the structured extraction record; a failure ends the row with no prediction.
stages.input_example: a payload whose selection lacks final_label
stages.paper_wording: Extractions that do not validate against the schema are recorded as failures rather than scored.

stages.name: Normalize every event
stages.operation: Convert each model event's source phrase into a comparable normalized rate; this runs over the whole ledger, not only the selected events.
stages.input_example: event 'about two seizures per month'
stages.paper_wording: Model-produced events are normalized to a common rate representation.

stages.name: Resolve the label from the model's selection
stages.operation: Read the model's selected_event_ids and final_kind and resolve the initial label from the corresponding normalized events.
stages.input_example: selected_event_ids ['evt_1'], final_kind 'frequency_rate'
stages.paper_wording: The model's selection is resolved into a label using the normalized form of the events it selected.
stages.notes: Representation, not selection: this stage renders the model's choice, it does not re-choose. If no selected event normalizes to a Gan label the row is recorded unscorable. row_trace.deterministic_selection retains both the model's own final_label and the resolved label so the two can be compared.

stages.name: Repair 1 - evidence-based label repair
stages.operation: Compare the resolved label with the model's quoted evidence span and rewrite the label when the evidence supports a different rate.
stages.input_type: resolved label plus selection evidence plus note text
stages.input_example: label '2 per month' with evidence 'two seizures in the past fortnight'
stages.paper_wording: A deterministic repair reconciles the label with the evidence span the model selected.

stages.name: Repair 2 - monthly diary
stages.operation: Derive a label from a month-by-month diary in the ledger and override the current label unless the existing label is preserved by the diary guard.
stages.input_type: StructuredExtractionRecord plus current label plus note text
stages.input_example: ledger listing 3, 2, and 4 seizures in three named months
stages.paper_wording: A deterministic repair converts month-by-month diary entries into a single rate.

stages.name: Repair 3 - usual interval
stages.operation: Convert a stated usual interval between seizures into a rate label when the ledger supports it.
stages.input_example: 'he usually goes about six weeks between seizures'
stages.paper_wording: A deterministic repair converts a stated usual interval into a rate.

stages.name: Repair 4 - typical rate over year-to-date
stages.operation: When the ledger holds both a typical recurring rate and a year-to-date total, prefer the typical recurring rate.
stages.input_example: 'typical pattern is a focal seizure monthly' alongside 'seven so far this year'
stages.paper_wording: A deterministic repair prefers a stated typical recurring rate over a year-to-date total.
stages.notes: Policy A1 in docs/research/shared/clinical_selection_policy_catalog_2026-07-31.md. Unlike its neighbours this repair is not gated by a repair_config flag; it runs whenever its precondition holds.

stages.name: Repair 5 - breakthrough seizures
stages.operation: Handle letters where the current burden is expressed as breakthrough seizures against an otherwise controlled background.
stages.input_example: 'seizure free apart from two breakthrough seizures this year'
stages.paper_wording: A deterministic repair resolves breakthrough-seizure phrasing against a controlled background.

stages.name: Repair 6 - non-epileptic events
stages.operation: Prevent events the ledger marks as non-epileptic from supplying the seizure-frequency answer.
stages.input_example: ledger holding both epileptic seizures and dissociative episodes
stages.output_example: the epileptic rate, not the combined rate
stages.paper_wording: A deterministic repair excludes events recorded as non-epileptic from the frequency answer.

stages.name: Repair 7 - residual jerks
stages.operation: Decide whether residual myoclonic jerks count toward the current seizure-frequency answer.
stages.input_type: StructuredExtractionRecord plus current label plus note text
stages.input_example: 'no generalised seizures but occasional morning jerks'
stages.output_example: the label the residual-jerk policy selects
stages.paper_wording: A deterministic repair applies the residual-jerk policy to the frequency answer.

stages.name: Repair 8 - post-change burst
stages.operation: Handle a burst of seizures that follows a named medication or lifestyle change, so a transient burst does not become the current rate.
stages.input_type: StructuredExtractionRecord plus current label plus note text
stages.input_example: 'after the dose reduction he had four seizures in a week, none since'
stages.paper_wording: A deterministic repair separates a post-change seizure burst from the settled current rate.

stages.name: Repair 9 - dated sequence
stages.operation: Derive a rate from a sequence of individually dated seizures and the window they span.
stages.input_type: StructuredExtractionRecord plus current label plus note text
stages.input_example: 'seizures on 3 January, 19 February and 28 March'
stages.paper_wording: A deterministic repair converts a dated seizure sequence into a rate over its observed window.

stages.name: Repair 10 - elapsed since anchor
stages.operation: When the selected answer is seizure-free since a dated anchor, count months from that date to the clinic date. A last-event rate rewrite can still be computed and then withheld by the sustained seizure-free guard.
stages.input_type: StructuredExtractionRecord plus current label plus note text
stages.input_example: 'Seizure-free since 27 March 2024' in a letter dated 29 September 2024
stages.paper_wording: A deterministic repair converts a seizure-free since-date into a month duration against the clinic date.

stages.name: Check the label is scorable
stages.operation: Parse the repaired label into a frequency record; an unparseable label is recorded as unscorable.
stages.input_example: 'a few a month'
stages.paper_wording: Labels that cannot be parsed into the benchmark representation are recorded as unscorable.

stages.name: Check evidence is an exact substring
stages.operation: Require the model's quoted selection evidence to appear verbatim in the note text.
stages.input_example: evidence 'about two seizures per month' against the note text
stages.paper_wording: Evidence is required to be an exact substring of the source note.
stages.notes: The evidence checked is the model's selection evidence, which the repair families do not rewrite. A repaired label can therefore carry evidence that motivated the model's original answer.

stages.name: Project to Purist and Pragmatic scoring
stages.operation: Map the predicted and gold monthly frequencies into the Purist and Pragmatic categories and compare.
stages.input_type: repaired label plus gold monthly frequency
stages.input_example: predicted 2.0 per month, gold 2.0 per month
stages.paper_wording: Predictions are scored under the Purist and Pragmatic category projections.

manifests.one_sentence: Nine independent deterministic extractors produce the all-nine prediction, while an explicit four-family projection defines the primary model comparison.
manifests.sixty_second: No model is involved. Nine entity-specific extractors run over the same note text: Diagnosis, Investigations, Onset, When Diagnosed, Birth History, Epilepsy Cause, Patient History, Prescription, and Seizure Frequency. Seizure Frequency is not a flat extractor - it runs its own staged deterministic sub-pipeline. The nine mention lists are concatenated and passed through mention-identity de-duplication, which is the only place where one extractor's output can suppress another's. The canonical orchestrator preserves that all-nine prediction and also materializes an explicit pure four-family comparison projection for Diagnosis, Seizure Frequency, Prescription, and Investigations. The all-nine result remains available for the secondary published-metric view; the primary model comparison uses only the named four-family projection.
manifests.prediction_owner: the nine deterministic extractors (stage exect.rules.extract_entities); the four-family projection is scorer-facing
manifests.scored_representation: An all-nine PredictedLetter plus an explicit four-family comparison projection, each scored under its named view.

stages.name: Extract seizure frequency
stages.operation: Run the staged deterministic seizure-frequency sub-pipeline, which has its own candidate, association, and temporal rule layers.
stages.input_example: "Seizures are now occurring about twice a month."
stages.output_example: one SeizureFrequency mention with state and rate attributes
stages.paper_wording: A staged deterministic sub-pipeline extracts seizure-frequency findings.
stages.notes: Seizure Frequency is the only family in this baseline with a multi-stage sub-pipeline of its own; the other eight are single extractors.

stages.name: Extract the other eight entities
stages.operation: Run the Diagnosis, Investigations, Onset, When Diagnosed, Birth History, Epilepsy Cause, Patient History, and Prescription extractors over the note text and concatenate their mentions with the seizure-frequency mentions.
stages.input_example: "Diagnosis: focal epilepsy. MRI brain was normal. Continue levetiracetam 500mg twice daily."
stages.paper_wording: Entity-specific deterministic extractors produce findings for nine clinical entities.
stages.notes: The extractors are independent: none reads another's output, so a Diagnosis miss cannot be recovered from a Prescription hit.

stages.name: De-duplicate mentions
stages.operation: Collapse mentions that share a mention identity, so the same finding produced by two extractors is counted once.
stages.input_example: two identical Diagnosis mentions of 'focal epilepsy'
stages.paper_wording: Findings are de-duplicated by mention identity before scoring.
stages.notes: The only stage where one extractor's output can remove another's. It removes duplicates, never disagreements.

stages.name: Score against gold
stages.operation: Keep the all-nine prediction intact, project a separate four-family comparison view, and match each named view to gold under the configured policy.
stages.input_example: predicted Diagnosis 'focal epilepsy' against gold 'focal epilepsy'
stages.output_example: Diagnosis P/R/F1 and an overall F1
stages.paper_wording: Predictions are scored by mention matching against the ExECTv2 gold annotations.
stages.notes: The canonical result exposes all-nine output and the pure four-family comparison projection. Never place the two overall numbers side by side without naming the view.

manifests.one_sentence: One structured model call proposes four-family findings, and the selected LLM-only view scores those findings before family-specific deterministic transforms.
manifests.sixty_second: The selected LLM-only lane shares one structured producer with the LLM-with-rules method. It builds the four-family prompt, makes or replays one model call, parses the event ledger, optionally performs a format-only retry for eligible local models, flattens events, and applies evidence and render-safety gates. Its selected prediction is the raw candidate view from that producer. It does not run seizure-frequency projection, Diagnosis reconciliation, Prescription rescue, or any other LLM-with-rules family transform. The old GEPA program remains named as a historical comparison rather than silently serving as the current selected entry point.
manifests.prediction_owner: the named model (stage exect.llm.model_call); deterministic stages only parse, represent, and gate its findings
manifests.scored_representation: The raw_candidate four-family PredictedLetter from the shared one-call producer, scored per entity and overall.

stages.name: Build the four-family prompt
stages.operation: Render the note text and the four-family event-ledger schema into the prompt input for one structured call.

stages.paper_wording: The selected LLM-only method starts from one structured four-family prompt.

stages.operation: One structured call returns candidate findings for Diagnosis, Seizure Frequency, Prescription, and Investigations, each with evidence.
stages.input_example: letter text plus the four-family schema
stages.paper_wording: A single language-model call proposes candidate findings for all four families.

stages.operation: Recover the structured event record and, when eligible, accept one format-only retry only after schema validation.
stages.input_example: an events list with a transport or JSON dialect error

stages.paper_wording: Malformed model output is handled at the transport and schema boundary.

stages.input_example: an event with family 'Diagnosis' and text 'focal epilepsy'
stages.output_example: a Diagnosis mention with its evidence span
stages.paper_wording: Model events are flattened into entity mentions without adding a deterministic extractor.

stages.name: Apply representation and evidence gates
stages.operation: Normalize closed-vocabulary attributes, require exact source evidence, and withhold mentions rejected by the shared render-safety gates.
stages.input_example: a mention whose evidence does not appear in the note
stages.output_example: the ungrounded mention is withheld and a gate warning is recorded
stages.paper_wording: The LLM-only candidate must pass evidence and render-safety gates before scoring.

stages.operation: Expose the producer's gated mentions as the selected LLM-only scoring view without applying the LLM-with-rules family transforms.
stages.input_example: four-family mentions from the shared producer
stages.output_example: the same four-family mentions with raw_candidate provenance
stages.paper_wording: The selected LLM-only view is the raw candidate from the one-call producer.

stages.paper_wording: The raw candidate view is scored by mention matching against ExECTv2 gold.

related_paths.note: The closed GEPA program is retained for historical comparison only; it is not the selected LLM-only entry point.

manifests.one_sentence: The model proposes findings for four families in one call; deterministic family transforms reconcile those findings into the final scored representation.
manifests.sixty_second: One structured call per letter asks the named model for candidate findings across Diagnosis, Seizure Frequency, Prescription, and Investigations. No deterministic extractor proposes findings and none is unioned in - that is the family-ownership rule from decision 0040. After the call, code parses and may make one format-only retry, flattens the model's events into ExECT mentions, projects the model's seizure-frequency facts into the required state representation, and suppresses a narrowly defined class of unsupported unknown states. Raw and scored findings are both registered in a finding store, so every later change stays attributable. Then one family transform runs per entity, and the four behave differently: Diagnosis applies the active standard dictionary to model findings; Seizure Frequency is a thin assembly over the earlier projection; Prescription applies dictionary-driven regimen processing with bounded correction; Investigations is a behavior-preserving adapter while its residual providers remain prompt-side. Every final finding must carry exact source evidence, and the scored views are then materialized.
manifests.prediction_owner: the named model proposes all four families (exect.llm_with_rules.model_call); four family transforms may change findings afterwards
manifests.scored_representation: A PredictedLetter of four-family mentions materialized into named score views; the primary view is clinical fact recovery (`clinical_headline`).

stages.name: Build the four-family prompt
stages.operation: Render the note text and the four-family event-ledger schema into the prompt input for one structured call.
stages.input_example: letter text plus letter id
stages.paper_wording: A single prompt requests candidate findings for four clinical families.

stages.name: Model proposes findings for four families
stages.operation: One structured call returns candidate findings for Diagnosis, Seizure Frequency, Prescription, and Investigations, each with evidence.
stages.input_example: letter text plus the four-family schema
stages.paper_wording: A single language-model call proposes candidate findings for all four families.
stages.notes: Decision 0040: the named model supplies all four families. No deterministic extractor may replace or be unioned into its result. This is what historical v08 did differently.

stages.name: Parse output, with format-only retry when eligible
stages.operation: Recover and repair the JSON payload, coerce legacy mention shapes into events, and for eligible local models make one format-only retry that is accepted only if it validates.
stages.input_example: an events list with one unclosed mention object
stages.output_example: a validated record with four events
stages.paper_wording: Malformed model output is repaired at the transport and schema level, with one format-only retry for local models.

stages.name: Flatten model events into mentions
stages.operation: Turn each model event into an ExECT mention with its entity, text, attributes, and evidence.
stages.input_example: an event with family 'Diagnosis' and text 'focal epilepsy'
stages.output_example: a Diagnosis mention 'focal epilepsy' with its evidence span
stages.paper_wording: Model events are flattened into entity mentions.

stages.name: Enrich attributes and apply render-safety gates
stages.operation: Attach CUI and canonical-phrase attributes, drop attribute values outside the closed vocabulary, drop seizure-frequency mentions that carry no frequency state, and drop modality-only Investigations duplicates.
stages.input_example: a SeizureFrequency mention with no state attributes; a Prescription mention with Frequency 'twice a day'
stages.output_example: the SeizureFrequency mention is dropped; the out-of-vocabulary Frequency value is removed
stages.paper_wording: Model mentions are enriched with concept identifiers and passed through render-safety gates before assembly.
stages.notes: Classed as clinical_meaning because it can remove a finding the model produced: a seizure-frequency mention without a frequency state is dropped outright. Its more common behaviour is representation enrichment, which is why it is easy to read as inert.

stages.name: Project seizure-frequency facts into the state representation
stages.operation: Convert the model's seizure-frequency facts into the state and ownership representation the ExECT scorer expects, including List 11 / range / interval / last-event encoding on emitted mentions, adding state attributes and named-type ownership the model did not supply.
stages.input_example: a mention 'seizure free since March' with no state attribute
stages.output_type: row of projected seizure-frequency mentions plus recorded actions
stages.output_example: the same mention carrying a seizure-free state and last-event date attributes
stages.paper_wording: Model-produced seizure-frequency facts are projected into the scored state representation, with every projection action recorded.
stages.notes: Named 'projection' but classed here as clinical_meaning: it can create the state representation that is scored, and it can add mentions from a candidate. Finding 4 of the 2026-07-30 review names this exact case. The selected setting is ablation='combined', which enables both the state and ownership projections.

stages.name: Suppress unsupported unknown states
stages.operation: Remove seizure-frequency findings whose state is unknown and unsupported under the narrowly defined suppression rule.
stages.input_example: a seizure-frequency mention with an unknown state and no supporting rate
stages.output_type: row with the suppressed mentions removed plus recorded actions
stages.output_example: the unknown-state mention is dropped and the action recorded
stages.paper_wording: A narrowly scoped deterministic rule suppresses unsupported unknown seizure-frequency states.
stages.notes: Removes model-produced findings. Suppression is a clinical change, not a filter on noise.

stages.name: Register raw and scored findings
stages.operation: Record both the raw and the scored surface of every finding in the finding store, with its producer, source lane, and ownership label.
stages.input_example: the Diagnosis row from the structured producer
stages.output_example: raw and scored surfaces for each of the four families
stages.paper_wording: Raw and scored findings are retained separately so every deterministic action stays attributable.
stages.notes: This stage is what makes component attribution possible: the model's raw output survives beside the reconciled output for every entity.

stages.name: Diagnosis family transform
stages.operation: Reconcile Diagnosis findings with the active standard dictionary; may rewrite, drop, or add bounded concepts.
stages.input_example: model Diagnosis findings such as 'epilepsy' with exact source evidence
stages.output_type: reconciled Diagnosis findings plus lens diagnostics
stages.output_example: model concepts after standard-dictionary rewrite, drop, or bounded addition
stages.paper_wording: A deterministic Diagnosis transform reconciles model findings against the active standard dictionary.
stages.notes: The active policy variant is 'default' (decision 0045). The 'combined' variant is archived development evidence and must not be the default for new runs. This is the family transform with the widest licence: it is the only one that can add a concept the model did not produce. Heading recovery and the generic epilepsy companion were zero-fire hooks in the decomposition and are retained only in historical artifacts, not the active lens.

stages.name: Seizure Frequency family transform
stages.operation: Assemble the already-projected and already-suppressed seizure-frequency findings; a thin transform that adds no further clinical change.
stages.input_type: Seizure Frequency findings in the store
stages.input_example: projected seizure-free findings from the sf producer
stages.output_example: the same findings in assembled form
stages.paper_wording: The Seizure Frequency transform assembles findings whose clinical projection has already been applied.
stages.notes: The clinical work for this family happened earlier, at exect.llm_with_rules.sf_state_projection and exect.llm_with_rules.sf_unknown_suppression. Reading the lens alone will understate what happened to Seizure Frequency.

stages.name: Prescription family transform
stages.operation: Normalize the surfaces the dictionary owns (generic drug name, canonical dose unit, dose value) and split an explicitly stated uneven once-daily regimen into one fact per dose.
stages.input_example: model finding 'levetiracetam 500mg BD'
stages.output_type: reconciled Prescription findings plus lens diagnostics
stages.output_example: a Prescription finding with normalized drug and dose attributes, or two findings where '400mg mane, 200mg nocte' was one
stages.paper_wording: A deterministic Prescription transform normalizes drug and dose surfaces and splits explicitly stated uneven daily regimens. It neither removes nor adds regimen findings.
stages.notes: The active policy variant is 'default' (decision 0045). Decision 0040 requires bounded correction here rather than deterministic substitution: the rules may correct the model, they may not replace it as the producer. v10 (2026-08-10): this transform no longer deletes model-selected regimens that read as planned or historical, and no longer adds dictionary residual regimens; both rules were measured net-harmful on dev140 across six models and were removed rather than guarded, so the stage can now only reshape a model finding, never remove or invent one. See docs/research/exectv2/prescription_lens_rule_decomposition_2026-08-10.md.

stages.name: Investigations family transform
stages.operation: Assemble model-selected Investigations findings without an additional dictionary rule pass.
stages.input_example: model-selected Investigations findings with exact source evidence
stages.output_example: the model-selected Investigations findings in assembled form
stages.paper_wording: The Investigations assembly stage preserves model-selected findings; residual providers remain available to prompt construction but are not consumed by this no-op lens.

stages.name: Require exact evidence for every finding
stages.operation: Reject the assembled letter if any final finding lacks evidence or carries evidence that is not an exact substring of the note.
stages.input_example: a Diagnosis finding whose evidence was paraphrased
stages.output_type: the assembled letter, or a ValueError
stages.output_example: ValueError: assembled 'EA0117' with 1 finding(s) without exact source evidence
stages.paper_wording: Every final finding is required to carry evidence that appears verbatim in the source note.
stages.notes: This gate raises rather than silently dropping. A family transform that invented an unevidenced concept fails the whole letter, which is why the Diagnosis transform's add licence is bounded in practice.

stages.name: Materialize the score views
stages.operation: Build the named prediction views - raw candidate, post-lens assembled findings, and clinical fact recovery - from the same assembled findings.
stages.input_example: four families of reconciled findings
stages.output_example: a clinical fact recovery (`clinical_headline`) view holding the unit keys
stages.paper_wording: Findings are materialized into named scoring views; the primary view is clinical fact recovery (`clinical_headline`).
stages.notes: One set of findings, several numbers. Naming the view is part of naming the result.

stages.name: Score against gold
stages.operation: Match the materialized view's mentions to gold annotations and report per-entity and overall precision, recall, and F1.
stages.input_example: clinical fact recovery view against the four-family gold
stages.output_example: a clinical fact recovery overall F1
stages.paper_wording: Predictions are scored by mention matching against the ExECTv2 gold annotations under the named view.
